newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-POOLEY GRABS ON-SHOT LEAD AT NISSAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-POOLEY GRABS ON-SHOT LEAD AT NISSAN OPEN.

text.p: Don Pooley, who is without a PGA Tour exemption, turned in another strong effort on Friday, shooting a three-under 68 to grab a one stroke lead at the midway point of the Nissan Open.
Pooley stood at seven-under par 135 through 36 holes, one better than Briton Nick Faldo, Mark O'Meara, Ted Tryba and overnight co-leader Scott Hoch.
Tryba fired the best round of the second-placed quartet with a five-under 66. O'Meara shot a 69, Faldo carded a 70 and Hoch managed even-par 71.
Craig Stadler and first-round co-leader Payne Stewart were two strokes off the pace at five-under 137.

Pooley began his season with a sponsor's exemption into the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic, where he finished tied for fifth, earning him entry into the Phoenix Open the following week, where he tied for 14th.
Another sponsors' exemption into the Tucson Classic led to a fifth place finish for Pooley.
"All parts of my game are working well," said the 45-year-old two-time winner on the PGA Tour.
"I'm very pleased with the way I'm playing. I got a lesson from Jim Flick before I started the year and made a couple of changes that made a huge difference in my ball-striking," Pooley explained.
"It's my best start in 22 years, I know that. I've been in the hunt everywhere I've played this year."
O'Meara's 69 kept him in contention for his third consecutive victory after wins at the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am and the Buick Invitational in his last two starts.
He earned his share of second place with the help of an eagle-3 on his 10th hole -- number one at the Riviera Country Club -- by holing a difficult bunker shot.

"That was a big plus," O'Meara said. "But I gave one back really quick. This was the kind of day when you'd make a charge and fall back, make a charge and fall back. It was a reflection of the golf course."
Faldo suffered a double-bogey 6 at the 12th hole, which prevented him from taking the lead.
"I hit a bad 3-wood under the trees," he said. "I tried a 5-iron and the ball went into the barranca. The ball landed on the rocks. The momentum went out of it a bit."
